newsitem.title: UK: British fuel demand up 5.3 pct in May-July.
newsitem.headline: British fuel demand up 5.3 pct in May-July.

text.p: British primary fuel demand rose by 5.3 percent to 48.8 million tonnes of oil equivalent in the three months from May to July compared to the same period last year, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said in a statement on Tuesday.
Natural gas use saw the biggest rise, by 22.7 percent, largely due to a significant increase in use for electricity generation.
However, the high gas demand in May was also due to colder weather than in the same period a year earlier.
Total motor fuel deliveries increased by two percent year on year, but diesel fuel jumped by 8.8 percent.
Fuel oil deliveries fell by 8.1 percent in May-July on the same period last year.
Unleaded petrol represented 66.8 percent of total motor spirit deliveries, 3.8 percent up on the year before.

Between mid-June and mid-July the price of leaded petrol, premium unleaded and diesel fuel fell by 0.1, 0.3 and 0.4 pence per litre respectively. Over the same period the price of super unleaded was unchanged.
The three month average price for May to July was 1.0 percent lower for leaded petrol, 6.1 percent higher for super unleaded petrol and 0.3 percent higher for premium unleaded petrol.
The average price for diesel increased by 1.6 percent over the same period.
